content.value: . The factorial n! of a positive number (integer) is defined by n! = n. (n − 1). (n - 2) ... 1, where 0! = 1 . Write a user-defined function that calculates the factorial n! of a number. For function name and arguments, use $y = f a c t ( x )$ , where the input argument x is the number whose factorial is to be calculated and the output argument y is the value x!. The function displays an error message if a negative or non-integer number is entered when the function is called. Do not use Octave built-in function ‘factorial.' Use fact with the following numbers: (i) 9! (ii) 8.5! (iii) 0! (iv) –5!
